parts.label: a
parts.technique: Mean and variance of grouped/discrete data
parts.reason: S2.3 explicitly covers calculation of mean, variance and standard deviation from data, including from frequency tables. This is just descriptive statistics of raw data, not requiring any distribution knowledge.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Justifying suitability of Poisson model
parts.reason: Requires knowledge that mean ≈ variance suggests Poisson distribution. Poisson distribution is not mentioned anywhere in the specification statements (only binomial and normal are covered under S4.1/S4.2), so this is out.

parts.label: c(i)
parts.technique: Poisson probability calculation
parts.reason: Uses Poisson distribution which is not part of the spec (only binomial and normal distributions listed under S4.1/S4.2).

parts.label: c(ii)
parts.technique: Poisson probability calculation
parts.reason: Same as above, requires Poisson distribution, not in spec.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Normal approximation to Poisson sum
parts.reason: Requires summing Poisson variables and using a Normal approximation to a Poisson-based quantity; Poisson is not in spec at all, so this cannot be done using in-spec methods.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: Binomial probability using previous Poisson-derived probability
parts.reason: Although this part uses a binomial distribution (S4.1), it depends entirely on the probability found in part (d), which is out of spec (Poisson-based). Since it only makes sense after an out-of-spec part, it is out.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Normal distribution, finding sigma from a percentile
parts.reason: S4.2 covers Normal distribution as a model and finding probabilities/parameters, including solving simultaneous equations for unknown parameters. This is a standard normal inverse calculation.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Binomial distribution probability, more than a value
parts.reason: S4.1 covers binomial distribution and calculating probabilities including cumulative probabilities.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Poisson approximation to binomial for repeated sampling
parts.reason: Requires use of a Poisson distribution, which is not mentioned in the specification statements at all (only binomial and normal are covered).

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Binomial modelling assumptions
parts.reason: S4.3 covers selecting an appropriate probability distribution with reasoning, including conditions for binomial suitability; this matches giving contextual assumptions for binomial model.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Critical region for binomial hypothesis test
parts.reason: S5.2 covers conducting a hypothesis test for the proportion in a binomial distribution, which includes finding critical regions; this is standard binomial hypothesis testing content.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Actual significance level from critical region
parts.reason: This follows directly from the S5.2 critical region calculation, a standard part of binomial hypothesis testing procedure.

parts.label: d
parts.technique: Interpreting result against critical region
parts.reason: Straightforward interpretation of hypothesis test result in context, part of S5.2 content.

parts.label: e
parts.technique: One-tailed binomial hypothesis test for proportion
parts.reason: S5.2 explicitly covers conducting a statistical hypothesis test for the proportion in a binomial distribution and interpreting results in context, including stating hypotheses in terms of p.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Sketching graph of a probability density function
parts.reason: S3.1 explicitly states 'No formal knowledge of probability density functions is required' and S4.2 excludes knowledge of the pdf; sketching an explicit pdf given by formula is out of spec.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Conditional probability calculation using a continuous pdf
parts.reason: Requires integrating a given probability density function to find probabilities, which relies on knowledge of pdfs explicitly excluded by S4.2/S3.1.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: E(X) of a continuous random variable via integration, combined with general E(aX+bY+c)
parts.reason: Requires computing E(G) by integrating g·f(g), i.e. derivation/calculation of the mean of a continuous random variable from a pdf; this is explicitly excluded knowledge (S4.2: derivation of the mean not required, and no pdf knowledge required generally). Also uses general linear combination of E(X) which is not covered.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Continuous uniform distribution variance
parts.reason: The continuous uniform distribution is not mentioned in any specification statement (S4.1 explicitly only covers discrete distributions and binomial; S4.2 covers only Normal). No statement covers continuous uniform distribution.

parts.label: b(i)
parts.technique: Continuous uniform distribution percentile
parts.reason: Same issue: continuous uniform distribution not covered by any statement in the specification.

parts.label: b(ii)
parts.technique: Continuous uniform distribution probability
parts.reason: Depends on continuous uniform distribution, not in spec, and also uses previous out-of-spec part's answer.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Continuous uniform distribution probability in modelling context
parts.reason: Relies on continuous uniform distribution model (part a/b), which is not covered anywhere in the specification statements.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Sampling distribution of a derived discrete random variable
parts.reason: Finding the full sampling/probability distribution of a discrete random variable built from binomial-type outcomes is not directly named in the statements. S3.1/S4.1 cover discrete distributions generally as models but constructing a sampling distribution table like this (a general discrete distribution derivation) goes beyond simple binomial probability calculation named in S4.1; however S4.1 does say 'understand and use simple, discrete probability distributions' which could cover this as long as calculation of mean/variance isn't required (it isn't here). This borders on being an 'S4.1 simple discrete probability distribution' problem, which is in spec.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Geometric-type distribution / binomial minimum n for P(Y≥1)>0.95
parts.reason: This is modelled as Y~B(n,p) and finding minimum n such that P(Y≥1)>0.95, which is a binomial calculation (S4.1) using logs, but depends on the probability found in part (a), which is a borderline/out topic depending on interpretation; given part (a) is judged in spec, this follows as binomial calculation.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Finding parameter using mode of continuous distribution via cdf differentiation
parts.reason: Requires differentiating a cumulative distribution function (cdf) to find a pdf and mode; knowledge of pdf/cdf for continuous random variables is explicitly excluded (S4.2: knowledge of pdf not required, derivation of cdf not required) and no statement covers general continuous distributions with cdfs.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Using F(1)=0 to find a constant in a cdf
parts.reason: Relies on cdf of a general continuous random variable, a topic not covered in the specification (S4.2 excludes pdf/cdf derivation, and no general continuous distribution content exists).

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Finding median from cdf of continuous random variable
parts.reason: Uses the cdf of a general continuous random variable to locate the median, which is not covered by any specification statement; S4.2 explicitly excludes pdf/cdf derivation and no general continuous r.v. topic exists.
